name: Standalone destination cross-reference
summary: A destination cross-reference identifies the receiving side of a diagram continuation relationship.
description: A destination cross-reference identifies the receiving side of a diagram continuation relationship. The destination marks where the referenced circuit or signal continues from its source. The relationship can span sheets without introducing another device or termination.
Check the source tag and the sheet/location reference after drawing changes. An apparently correct arrow can still point to a stale or unrelated continuation.
readingNotes: Check the source reference and the signal or circuit identity on both sheets.
A continuation reference does not imply a physical terminal or cable splice.
drawingChecklist: Identify the associated device, circuit or diagram boundary.
Check the source reference and the signal or circuit identity on both sheets.
Cross-reference the equipment data, terminal mapping or operating-state legend needed to interpret the form.
distinction: A continuation reference does not imply a physical terminal or cable splice.
